title: Measuring spectral reflectance and transmittance of large leaves using SVC DC-R/T Integrating Sphere
author: Etienne Laliberté
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.p8pdrvn

steps.title: Prepare Spectroradiometer and Software
steps.instruction: Set up the spectroradiometer hardware and software configuration.

substeps.instruction: Install the integrating sphere onto the spectroradiometer following the SVC integrating sphere manual p. 6-16.
Power the spectroradiometer and warm up for >15 min; record the start time.
Ensure the spectroradiometer is connected to the computer via Bluetooth (default password for SVC HR-1024i is hr1024i).
Go to Control > Setup Instrument to connect the spectroradiometer via the appropriate virtual COM port.
In Control > Overlap / Matching Settings: Select 'Preserve Overlapped Detector Data' and set 'Matching Type' to 'None'.
Choose the RAW DN optic, select 5 sec scan time, select Auto Integration, ensure date/time are correct, and check Integration Scales Raw DN Data.
Select auto-save mode via File > Data Options > Auto Save.

Create a new working folder in the shared 'spectra' Google Drive CABO folder (named YYYYstarted-YourLastName-Degree-University) and a subfolder named YYYY-MM-DD-SiteID-SpectroradiometerSerialNumber; keep the default file base name (e.g., grMMDDYY).

steps.title: Align Lamp and Install Light Traps
steps.instruction: Position the lamp and secure light traps for reflectance measurements.

substeps.instruction: Position the lamp over the sphere primary light entrance port and secure it in the locked position (use the slotted heat shield to avoid burns).
Check lamp alignment by placing a thin piece of paper at the exit of the reflectance sample port to ensure the beam under-fills and is centered; if not, follow the SVC manual p. 29-32.
Screw the tethered light trap onto the reflectance port sample holder.
Screw the untethered light trap onto the transmission port sample holder.

steps.title: Collect Reflectance Reference and Stray Light Scans
steps.instruction: Establish the reference and stray light radiance values for reflectance mode.

substeps.instruction: Position leaf #1 over the transmission port with the adaxial (upper) surface facing into the sphere, avoiding the large midrib vein and positioning it halfway between the mid-rib and margin, and halfway between the tip and base.
Collect a 'Reference Scan' (R ref).
Remove leaf #1 from the transmission port sample holder.
Remove the tethered calibrated Spectralon® reflectance standard from the reflectance port (if present).
Place the tethered calibrated Spectralon® reflectance standard over the transmission port sample holder so the light beam shines directly on the reflective surface facing into the sphere.
Collect a 'Target Scan' (R str) and save the file.

steps.title: Measure Adaxial Reflectance of Leaves
steps.instruction: Collect target radiance scans for the adaxial surface of multiple leaves.

substeps.instruction: Position leaf #1 over the reflectance port with the adaxial (upper) surface facing into the sphere, targeting the same area as the reference radiance and avoiding the midrib vein.
Collect a 'Target Scan' (R tar,1) and save the file.
Repeat the positioning and scanning process for leaves #2 through #6, saving each as R tar,2 through R tar,6.

steps.title: Configure System for Transmittance Mode
steps.instruction: Reconfigure the lamp and ports for transmittance measurements.

substeps.instruction: Position leaf #1 over the reflectance port with the abaxial (lower) side facing the inside of the sphere.
Remove the tethered calibrated Spectralon® reflectance standard from the reflectance port.
Remove the light trap from the transmission port sample holder.
Position the lamp over the sphere transmission port and secure it in the locked position.
Install the Spectralon® plug over the primary light port, ensuring the curved plug matches the sphere curvature.
Remove leaf #1 from the reflectance port sample holder (leaving the light trap on).
Gently pull the lamp and transmission sample holder away from the sphere.

steps.title: Measure Adaxial Transmittance of Leaves
steps.instruction: Collect target radiance scans for the transmittance of multiple leaves.

substeps.instruction: Place leaf #1 over the transmission port with the abaxial (lower) surface facing into the sphere, targeting the same area as the reflectance radiance and avoiding the midrib vein.
Release the transmission sample holder and move the lamp back to its locked position.
Collect a 'Target Scan' (T tar,1) and save the file.
Repeat the positioning and scanning process for leaves #2 through #6, saving each as T tar,2 through T tar,6.

steps.title: Collect Final Reference and Stability Scans
steps.instruction: Perform final scans to determine transmittance reference and system stability.

substeps.instruction: Remove leaf #6 from the transmission sample port holder.
Collect a 'Reference Scan' (T ref) in the current configuration.
Remove leaf #6 from the reflectance sample port holder.
Place the tethered calibrated Spectralon® reflectance standard over the reflectance port facing into the sphere.
Position leaf #1 over the transmission port with the adaxial (upper) surface facing into the sphere (following standard positioning rules).
Collect a 'Target Scan' to assess system stability in reflectance mode.
Remove leaf #1 from the transmission port sample holder.
Position leaf #1 over the reflectance port with the abaxial (lower) side facing the inside of the sphere (following standard positioning rules).
Collect a 'Target Scan' to assess system stability in transmittance mode.
